answers.why: Israel is the holy people who followed the LORD in the wilderness and whose devourers face judgment.
The address includes all the families of the house of Israel.
Israel is the plundered people whose land and cities are devastated in the following verse.
The house of Israel includes their kings, princes, priests, and prophets.
Judah is addressed as having cities and numerous false gods.
Israel is identified with the LORD's people who say they will no longer come to him.
Israel is personified as an unfaithful woman worshipping on hills, with Judah as her sister.
Judah is personified as the treacherous sister who witnesses Israel's unfaithfulness.
Israel is personified as an adulterous wife whom the LORD sends away.
Judah is Israel's personified sister who also commits religious adultery.
Judah is the treacherous sister whose return to the LORD is insincere.
Israel's national unfaithfulness is compared with that of treacherous Judah.
Judah is the treacherous nation compared with backsliding Israel.
The proclamation toward the north calls backsliding Israel to return and addresses its members in the plural.
The collective speakers confess that Israel's salvation is in the LORD their God.
